name: mc_build
title: Build
description:
Places blocks in bulk: cuboid fills, individual blocks (with sign text), rendered lettering (`text`), generated cell sets (`cells`/`cellsFile`), saved blueprints and decorative `entities`. Up to 500,000 blocks per call; runs across ticks without lagging players.

WHEN TO USE: any placement beyond a handful of blocks - buildings, terrain, clearing, roads. Prefer few large `fills`. Use `blocks` for oriented or stateful details with the full state string, e.g. `minecraft:oak_stairs[facing=north,half=bottom]`; `text` for lettering larger than a sign (never hand-place letters); `entities` for paintings, item frames and armor stands (journalled and snapshotted, unlike mc_command summon); `blueprint:{id,palette?}` for a saved mc_blueprint design; `cells` [[x,y,z,"state"],...] (up to 50,000 inline) or `cellsFile` (staged upload or mc_export file) for generated content - equal neighbours are merged into boxes for you.
WHEN NOT TO USE: to read the world (mc_survey, mc_inspect); to run a server command (mc_command).

COORDINATES: X east, Z south, Y up. Positions are absolute unless `transform` is given; then every position is local: mirror first, rotate clockwise viewed from above, then add the origin. States, filters and text geometry transform too; sign strings stay readable, mirrored block lettering has mirrored glyphs. `from`/`to` are inclusive corners in any order. Execution order is ALWAYS fills -> text -> blocks -> entities, regardless of JSON key order; array order applies within each phase. A later block overwrites an earlier air fill: to keep an opening, omit conflicting blocks or place final minecraft:air entries at the end of blocks. Supply both halves of doors and beds. A blueprint applies component mirror/rotation, then instance positions and repetition, then `transform`, and cannot be combined with fills/blocks/text. `cells`/`cellsFile` are absolute and cannot be combined with fills, blocks, text, blueprint, transform or preflight; up to 2,000,000 cells are split into parts that are all validated and protection-checked before the first write and built under one journal id (if a part fails, the earlier parts stay and the reply gives `resume`). `entities` cannot be combined with blueprint or cells. Blocks are placed without physics (see `liquids`); connectable blocks get a shape-only update (see `connect`). For a sign, add a `sign` object to a `blocks` entry whose block is a sign (a wall sign goes in the air block in front of the wall).

SIDE EFFECTS: permanently modifies the world, except with dryRun:true (read-only JSON report; mc_plan adds an image). Every phase is structurally validated before the first snapshot or write; preflight:true also rejects door/bed pairing and support failures. Every writing call is journalled: the reply names a journal id that mc_restore {journal} undoes selectively, including sign text and placed or removed entities (not inventories); snapshot:true also saves the affected region first. A deny protected region (mc_protect) rejects the whole call unless named in `override`; a warn region adds a warning. Limits per call: 500,000 blocks, 1,024 chunks, one world; an over-limit request changes nothing. The reply lists WARNINGS for unsupported blocks (ladders, torches, signs, doors, carpets...); fix them before reporting the build done.

cells.description: Absolute [x, y, z, "block_state"] cells, up to 50,000.

cellsFile.description: Name of a finalized staged upload (mc_blueprint stage/finalize) or an mc_export file, without extension.

resume.description: Token from a stopped cells build: repeats the same call from that part.

detailed.description: Add per-fill and per-text-entry results. Default false.

override.description: Protected region names this call may write into anyway; no wildcards. Only when the user explicitly asks.

label.description: Name for this call's journal entry; mc_snapshot journal-list can filter by it.

journal.description: Default true. false skips the undo record; only for throwaway tests.

dryRun.description: Read-only final-scene report; no snapshots or writes.

preflight.description: Reject the build before writing if door/bed pairing, support or neighbour checks fail. Structural validation always runs.

world.description: World name; default: the configured default world.

blueprint.description: Build a saved mc_blueprint document. The reply ends with a "Blueprint:" line naming its tags and journal id.

palette.description: Role -> block state. Precedence: component defaults < document palette < these overrides < instance palette; $role[property=value] overrides bound properties.

transform.description: Local frame for all positions: mirror, then rotate clockwise viewed from above (90 maps local +X to world +Z), then translate. Paired blocks are not created for you.

rotation.description: Clockwise degrees viewed from above. Default 0.

mirror.description: Local axis to negate before rotating. Default none.

to.description: Opposite inclusive corner; order does not matter.

block.description: Block state, e.g. "minecraft:oak_log[axis=y]"; orientation rules as on blocks[].block.

mode.description: "replace" (default) overwrites everything; "keep" fills only air; "outline" places a 1-block shell; "hollow" places the shell and clears the inside; "walls" places only the four vertical sides (add floor and roof separately). "walls" does not clear grass, flowers or snow inside: on terrain, clear the inside with an air fill first.

filter.description: Replace only cells matching this state (unspecified properties match any), e.g. "minecraft:air" to fill only the empty cells of a crater.

block.description: Full block state, e.g. "minecraft:oak_stairs[facing=north,half=bottom]". Attached blocks (ladder, wall_torch, wall_sign, wall_banner, lever/button with face=wall): `facing` points AWAY from the support (a ladder on a room's west wall is facing=east) and the block goes in the air cell beside the wall - never replace the wall itself. `torch` stands on the block below. Doors: the panel sits on the face OPPOSITE `facing`; half=lower at y and half=upper at y+1 with identical other properties; hinge picks the swing side. Stairs: you walk up toward `facing`; half=top is upside down. Beds: part=foot at pos, part=head one block toward `facing`. Chests/furnaces: `facing` is the front. Slabs: type=bottom|top|double. Chests: with connect on, adjacent single chests with the same facing pair automatically; with connect:false give explicit type=left/right halves and never guess handedness.

sign.description: Text for this entry's sign block (*_sign or *_hanging_sign); front and/or back.

front.description: Up to 4 lines, top to bottom, at most 64 characters each.

back.description: Up to 4 lines, top to bottom, at most 64 characters each.

color.description: Dye colour of the text, default "black".

waxed.description: Waxed (players cannot edit it). Default false.

text.description: Lettering rendered as blocks: a 5x7 font for ASCII; other scripts (CJK...) through Java fonts, 12 rows tall. Use it for any word made of blocks instead of hand-placed letters. Counts against the same limits as fills.
1-64 characters, up to 4 lines separated by \n (1-row gap). Non-ASCII fails the call if the server has no font for it.

pos.description: Bottom-left block (align "left") or bottom-centre block (align "center") of the first line, in the text's own plane; for facing "up", the ground cell it lies on.

block.description: Block state for the letters; solid opaque blocks read best.

align.description: "left" (default) or "center" (pos is the bottom-centre; an uneven extra block goes toward the reading direction). Use "center" to anchor on a player's position.

background.description: Optional block state for a solid plaque over the text's bounding box. Without it only the letters are written and the gaps are left untouched.

facing.description: Side it is read from: "south" (default), "north", "east", "west" (upright), or "up" (flat on the ground, letter tops toward north).

scale.description: Each font pixel becomes an NxN square. Default 1 (a capital is 5x7 blocks); 2-4 to read from afar.

spacing.description: Blank columns between glyphs before scale. Default 1.

snapshot.description: Save the affected bounding box first (block states, sign text, decorative entities). Default false.

connect.description: Shape-only update so panes, fences, walls, bars, stairs and redstone wire connect to their neighbours. Default true; false skips it.

entities.description: Up to 256 decorative entities, placed after all blocks. Each needs `type` and `pos` (local under `transform`; facings and yaw turn with it). painting: `facing` (the side the picture shows on) and `variant` (e.g. "kebab"); `pos` is the lower-left cell as the viewer sees it (lower-right under a mirror transform), in the air in front of a solid wall. item_frame/glow_item_frame: `facing` (also up/down; it hangs on the block opposite), optional `item`, `rotation` 0-7, `fixed` (default true), `invisible`. armor_stand: `pos` is the feet cell; optional `yaw` (0 south, 90 west), `equipment` {head,chest,legs,feet,mainHand,offHand: item id}, `pose` {head,body,leftArm,rightArm,leftLeg,rightLeg: [x,y,z] degrees}, `small`, `invisible`, `noGravity`. An identical entity already there is left as is; one that cannot be placed is reported and the rest are still placed.

entityMode.description: "add" (default), or "replace-in-box": first remove the Ashlar-placed entities of the requested types inside `entityBox`. Hand-placed entities, marker armor stands, mobs and players are never removed.

entityBox.description: {from, to} inclusive corners for "replace-in-box" (local under `transform`), at most 1,000,000 blocks.

liquids.description: "static" (default): water and lava never flow. "flow": water and lava in this call's fills and blocks behave like hand-placed sources (fountains, waterfalls, streams). Flow has its own smaller cap: use it for a few sources, not to fill a lake.
